references.text: Jesus says that the gate is narrow and the way is small that leads to life, and few find it. This is the closest parallel to the question of whether few are saved ([ref:Matt 7:14|Matthew 7:14]).
Jesus says that many are called but few are chosen – a statement that directly addresses the question of how many will be saved ([ref:Matt 22:14|Matthew 22:14]).

The disciples ask, "Who then can be saved?" after Jesus' words that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter God's kingdom. The question shares the same underlying concern as in Luke 13:23 ([ref:Matt 19:25|Matthew 19:25]).

Jesus' answer to the question: "Strive to enter through the narrow door! For many, I tell you, will try to enter but will not be able." This is the direct continuation and response to the question in verse 23 ([ref:Luk 13:24|Luke 13:24]).
The Lord added those who were being saved (οἱ σῳζόμενοι) to the church day by day. The expression "those who were being saved" is the same as used in Luke 13:23 ([ref:Apg 2:47|Acts 2:47]).

Isaiah prophesies that although the people of Israel are countless as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will turn back. This Old Testament perspective that only a remnant will be saved forms the background for the question in Luke 13:23 ([ref:Jes 10:22|Isaiah 10:22]).
Paul quotes Isaiah saying that only a remnant of Israel will be saved, which connects to the question of whether few are saved ([ref:Rom 9:27-28|Romans 9:27-28]).
Paul speaks about how even in present times there is a remnant chosen by grace, thus linking to the theme of the salvation of the few ([ref:Rom 11:5-6|Romans 11:5-6]).

Peter asks: "If the righteous are saved with difficulty, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?" The question reflects the same concern as in Luke 13:23 about how difficult salvation is ([ref:1 Pet 4:18|1 Peter 4:18]).

Jesus calls his disciples "little flock" and says that the Father has decided to give them the kingdom. The expression "little flock" suggests that those who are saved are relatively few ([ref:Luk 12:32|Luke 12:32]).
